vocabulary.example: Read “reach” and “react” aloud. You probably have little difficulty with either. But how would you explain why the letters “ea” make different sounds in each word? In reach, the letters work together to represent one sound, the long “e” sound. In react, the word’s structure changes how we group the letters: it divides into re + act. The “e” ends the prefix re-, and the a starts act, so they represent separate vowel sounds. A prefix is a meaningful word part added at the beginning of a word. Recognising such parts draws on morphology: knowledge of word structure.

parts.text: This is why explicit language knowledge matters. The teacher needs to understand how sounds, letters and word structure

, then use that understanding to interpret the student’s attempt and choose a useful explanation. Teachers need the knowledge and practical skill to decide what to teach next. Being able to read fluently ourselves does not automatically

us to do that.

What our research found

In our study of teachers working in the first three years of primary school in Scotland, 122 teachers completed a knowledge assessment. Their weakest area was phonics, decoding and encoding: understanding relationships between letters and sounds and using them to read and spell. On

, they answered 53% of questions in this area correctly. This knowledge helps teachers explicitly teach word reading and spelling, two skills that dyslexia affects.

One teacher from our study captured the

: “I can identify when readers are struggling but do not yet have the right skills and experience to help them.” They described “feeling deflated and like I’m failing”.

The concern

beyond Scotland. A 2026 meta-analysis of 143 studies, most conducted in English-speaking countries, identified gaps in teachers’ language and literacy knowledge.

Building knowledge and the skill to use it

Teacher education should make this expertise an explicit part of preparation. Trainees need to understand sound–letter relationships and word structure (

) explicitly. They also need to learn how to assess what a child understands and decide what to teach next.

There is evidence that preparation can build this knowledge. A review of 20 studies of teacher preparation and

found that programmes allowing teachers to apply their learning under expert guidance produced the largest gains in teacher knowledge. It also reported preliminary evidence of benefits for children’s word reading. Knowledge development and supported practice

together.

Our study, Book Buddies, offers one example. In this Scottish programme, trainee teachers combined explicit language and literacy coursework with tutoring children in their second year of primary school who needed

reading support. Over ten weeks, each child received two individual sessions a week. Trainees rehearsed lessons with peers, used assessment to choose a starting point, monitored progress weekly and adjusted lessons with feedback from teacher
. Before-and-after assessments showed gains in trainees’ literacy knowledge and reported confidence, and in children’s word reading.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Better preparation for teachers is central to supporting pupils with dyslexia.
Science curricula often overlook women whose work helped shape scientific knowledge.
Adults' responses to risk and mess can limit the benefits children gain from outdoor play.
A long-term study links public prekindergarten attendance to better later educational outcomes.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: In this article, we explain what teachers need to know, what we learned from our research, and why it matters for dyslexia.

questions.prompt: Which approach is described as particularly helpful for children at risk of dyslexia?
options: Avoiding all discussion of written language
Assuming that every child has identical reading needs
questions.explanation: 第 3 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: Research suggests that children at risk of dyslexia benefit most from such high-quality explicit teaching.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 7?
options: Working out what to teach so the child can read similar words independently takes a different kind of expertise.
The teacher needs to understand how sounds, letters and word structure interact, then use that understanding to interpret the student’s attempt and choose a useful explanation.
Helping requires teaching that targets the skills involved, and that depends on teachers understanding how spoken and written language works.
In react, the word’s structure changes how we group the letters: it divides into re + act.
questions.explanation: 定位第 7 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: The teacher needs to understand how sounds, letters and word structure interact, then use that understanding to interpret the student’s attempt and choose a useful explanation.
